item.title: KEPCO Data Breach Exposes 1.5 Million Individuals
item.description:
KEPCO Data Breach Exposes 1.5 Million Individuals

A threat actor breached the internal network of Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO), exposing details of more than 1.5 million individuals.

🔍 Overview

  • KEPCO, South Korea’s main electric power company, detected an attack on November 20.
  • The breach exposed customer, employee, and contractor data.
  • The attack was detected when unauthorized access was confirmed to KEPCO ON and SRM systems.

⚙️ Key details

  • The following data was exposed:
    • For 650,487 KEPCO ON customers: names, ID information, phone numbers, addresses, bank names, bank account numbers, account holder names, card issuers, card numbers, cardholder names, and electricity charge and billing information.
    • For 426,827 company representatives: names, ID information, email addresses, and company addresses.
    • For 442,934 KEPCO employees: names, affiliation, employee ID number, mobile phone number, email address, company phone number.
  • The data breach resulted from “advanced technologies as AI,” but specific details about the initial access method or attack chain were not shared.
  • KEPCO is notifying exposed individuals directly, has filed a report with the data protection authorities, and is coordinating with government and financial authorities to block abuse.

💡 Why it matters

  • Potentially exposed individuals are warned that the exposed information could be used for targeted phishing and impersonation.
  • They are advised to report any attempts to the police or Korea’s Internet and Security Agency.
  • It is recommended to avoid installing unknown apps, entering information into suspicious forms, and sharing sensitive data or verification codes over calls or texts.

🔗 Attribution

  • A threat actor using the “Noiem” alias has claimed the attack and advertised the breach on a hacker forum on November 19.
  • South Korea’s Personal Information Protection Commission separately confirmed that KEPCO received an email from a hacker claiming data theft on November 19.
  • While these claims match the available evidence, attribution to Noiem remains unconfirmed.

#KEPCO #DataBreach #CyberSecurity #SouthKorea #CriticalInfrastructure

Source: South Korea’s power giant KEPCO confirms data breach impacting 1.5 million

item.title: Samsung Expands Pyeongtaek Semiconductor Complex to Reclaim Lead in AI Memory Chips
item.description:
Samsung Expands Pyeongtaek Semiconductor Complex to Reclaim Lead in AI Memory Chips

Samsung is building a massive new semiconductor manufacturing complex in Pyeongtaek, South Korea, as it attempts to reclaim its lead in the global memory chip market. The build-out in the farming city south of Seoul comes as the company predicts demand for memory chips will continue to surge through 2028 due to the AI boom.

🔍 Overview

The Pyeongtaek campus covers an area approximately the size of New York City’s Central Park and operates as a sprawling chipmaking complex where rice paddies abut the industrial facilities.

  • Operational Status: Three fabs already operate around the clock.
  • Current Expansion: A fourth fab is currently coming online.
  • Restarted Construction: Construction of a fifth fab was halted in 2024 during a drop in memory demand but restarted when AI-driven demand increased.

⚙️ Key details

The construction site employs hundreds of women, many of whom serve as spotters to ensure safety around heavy equipment.

Role Responsibilities Daily Pay
Safety Officer Overseeing crews responsible for building cable ducts 140,000 won ($97)
Spotter Walking ahead of heavy equipment 140,000 won ($97)

💡 Why it matters

Samsung is using the Pyeongtaek expansion to address shifts in the global semiconductor landscape:

  • Market Competition: Domestic rival SK Hynix has pulled ahead in the global market for high-bandwidth memory models used in Nvidia’s AI accelerators.
  • Foundry Dominance: Taiwanese chipmaker TSMC currently dominates the foundry business, manufacturing chips designed by other companies.
  • Future Demand: Samsung forecasts that the surge in demand for memory chips will persist through 2028.

#Samsung #Semiconductors #AIChips #SouthKorea

Source: A visit to Samsung’s massive new semiconductor hub
